rationale: Lycopolitan dialectal/scribal variant of ⲍⲱⲱϩ (= Sahidic ϩⲱⲱϥ), the reflexive/intensive pronoun. Glossary already lists ⲍⲱⲱϩ; ⲍⲱⲙϩ adds an orthographic variant (medial ⲙ for second ⲱ) likely reflecting nasalization or scribal substitution. Same function: 'himself, also.'

Hapax in this corpus. Context (collocation with ⲁϩⲉⲉϥ 'stand him' and ⲛ̄ⲣⲙⲍⲉ 'as freeman') points to a causative or co-verb of establishment in freedom. Possibly Lyc. compound ⲟⲩⲱϩ-ⲓⲁ + 3sg.m suffix 'set him on a foot' or related establishment-verb. Confidence very low; flagged for parallels.

The form ⲁϩⲣ̄- in ⲁϩⲣ̄ⲁⲓⲥⲑⲁⲛⲉ (line 22) parallels the standard Lyc. ⲁϥⲣ̄- 'he did' (with Greek loanword + verbalizing ⲣ̄-). The ⲁϩ-spelling for the perfect 3sg.m. ⲁϥ- is consistent with this manuscript's Lycopolitan features (cf. ⲁϩⲭⲓ 'he received,' ⲁϩϯ 'he gave' on the same page). Document as orthographic variant of perfect 3sg.m.
